claim: ntfy is a simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service that sends notifications to phone or desktop via PUT/POST without signup or fees, written mainly in Go, with ~30.7k GitHub stars.
quote: ntfy is a simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. It allows you to send notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts from any computer, without having to sign up or pay any fees.

claim: ntfy lets you publish to named topics over HTTP PUT/POST and subscribe via its own open-source Android/iOS apps or the web; it can also act as a UnifiedPush distributor.
quote: ntfy.sh | Push notifications to your phone or desktop via PUT/POST

claim: ntfy implements UnifiedPush, enabling push notifications without Google Firebase Cloud Messaging, acting as a distributor for UnifiedPush-compatible apps like Element and FluffyChat.
quote: ntfy implements UnifiedPush, the standard which makes it possible to send and receive push notifications without using Google's Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) service.

claim: Gotify is a simple self-hosted server for sending (REST API) and receiving (WebSocket) messages in real-time, with a web UI, its own Android app, and CLI; written in Go with ~15.1k GitHub stars.
quote: A simple server for sending and receiving messages in real-time per WebSocket. (Includes a sleek web-ui)

claim: Gotify's Android app subscribes to the server's WebSocket message stream and creates push notifications on newly received messages, running independently of cloud push services.
quote: subscribing/receiving messages via a web socket connection

claim: Apprise is a notification routing library and CLI that dispatches one message to almost all popular notification services via a common syntax; it lists Gotify, Pushover, Telegram, Discord, Slack and others as targets, with ~16.7k GitHub stars.
quote: Apprise allows you to send a notification to almost all of the most popular notification services available to us today such as: Telegram, Discord, Slack, Amazon SNS, Gotify, etc.

claim: Apprise-API is a lightweight REST microservice wrapping the Apprise library, acting as a gateway that fans out one HTTP request to 130+ downstream services via stateless or stateful (stored config key) modes.
quote: A lightweight REST framework that wraps the Apprise Notification Library ... send notifications to more than 130+ services ... an incredibly lightweight gateway to Apprise

claim: ntfy ships as image binwiederhier/ntfy; the Docker image does not contain a server.yml so users must create and mount /etc/ntfy/server.yml plus a /var/cache/ntfy volume for the cache.db.
quote: the Docker image does not contain a `/etc/ntfy/server.yml` file ... docker run -v /var/cache/ntfy:/var/cache/ntfy -p 80:80 -it binwiederhier/ntfy serve --cache-file /var/cache/ntfy/cache.db

claim: Gotify runs from gotify/server (or ghcr.io/gotify/server); a single /app/data volume holds the SQLite database, images and certs and should be backed up, with default admin password set via GOTIFY_DEFAULTUSER_PASS.
quote: docker run -p 80:80 -v /var/gotify/data:/app/data gotify/server ... The /app/data directory stores the SQLite database, application images, and certificate files. This directory should be included in a backup.

claim: LinuxServer publishes lscr.io/linuxserver/apprise-api:latest, a rootless PUID/PGID image on port 8000 with /config persistence and APPRISE_ATTACH_SIZE control.
quote: image: lscr.io/linuxserver/apprise-api:latest ... environment: PUID=1000 PGID=1000 TZ=Etc/UTC APPRISE_ATTACH_SIZE=0 ... volumes: /config /attachments

claim: ntfy auth uses an auth-file SQLite db with auth-default-access (set deny-all for private), admin/user roles, granular per-topic ACLs and tk_-prefixed access tokens, managed via ntfy user add / ntfy access / ntfy token add CLI or declarative server.yml.
quote: auth-default-access: Fallback permission ... read-write (default), read-only, write-only, or deny-all ... ntfy user add [--role=admin] USERNAME ... Token format: Must start with tk_ and be 32 characters

claim: Gotify auth is application-token based: an application is created in the WebUI/REST-API and its token is passed as a query param to push messages, with only the creating user able to see them.
quote: To authenticate as an application you need the application token ... curl "https://push.example.de/message?token=<apptoken>" -F "title=my title" ... Only the user who created the application is able to see its messages.

claim: A homelab comparison rates Gotify's install as easy with ~5 env vars while ntfy needs more setup plus CLI user/ACL management, but finds ntfy more complete with finer permissions.
quote: The installation was not hard but required a bit of more setup for Ntfy, and Easy installation process for Gotify ... Ntfy additionally requires CLI commands to manage users and permissions

claim: Gotify uses under 50 MB of RAM and runs on the smallest VPS or Raspberry Pi, with a typical Docker memory limit of 128M.
quote: Gotify is extremely lightweight, using less than 50 MB of RAM, so it runs happily on even the smallest VPS or Raspberry Pi ... memory: 128M

claim: ntfy publishes via HTTP PUT/POST with five priority levels (1=min to 5=max) set via X-Priority header, tags/emoji via X-Tags, and up to three action buttons (view, http, broadcast, copy).
quote: Priority 5 max/urgent: Really long vibration bursts... Priority 1 min: The notification will be under the fold in 'Other notifications'. Set via X-Priority header. Up to three actions per notification. view, http, broadcast, copy.

claim: ntfy provides user/admin roles and ACLs with read-write/read-only/write-only/deny permissions per topic pattern (wildcards supported), access tokens (tk_ prefix, 32 chars), and auth-default-access to make an instance private (deny-all).
quote: read-write (rw)... read-only (read, ro)... write-only (write, wo)... deny (none): neither publishing nor subscribing... auth-default-access... deny-all: Private instance... Tokens must start with tk_ and be 32 characters long.

claim: Gotify uses two token types: appToken (applications that send messages) and clientToken (clients that receive messages and manage the server, e.g. the Android app), transmitted via X-Gotify-Key header, token query param, or Bearer Authorization; priority is an integer (default 5).
quote: clientToken (a client is something that receives messages... for example this token should be used for an Android app) and appToken (an application is something that sends messages)... transmitted in a header named X-Gotify-Key, in a query parameter named token or through... Bearer

claim: Apprise is a send-only notification relay (it does not receive notifications) that normalizes to popular services via standardized service://credentials@host/target URLs, with OR/AND tagging, local-file and remote-URL attachments, and YAML/text config files.
quote: Apprise is a send-only notification relay—it does not receive notifications itself... service://credentials@host/target... discord://webhook_id/webhook_token... OR logic: -g devops -g admin... AND logic: -g devops,critical... Attachment Support: Yes... YAML and plain text formats supported

claim: Apprise supports notifications to roughly 143 services (commonly cited as 100+), including Discord, Telegram, Slack, ntfy, Gotify, Pushover, email (SMTP), SMS (Twilio/Vonage), Matrix, and Microsoft Teams.
quote: Apprise supports sending notifications to 143 services including email, chat platforms, and SMS providers.

claim: On iOS, ntfy cannot use background WebSocket/JSON-stream connections so all push must traverse APNs; self-hosted servers relay poll requests through ntfy.sh upstream (self-hosted ntfy to ntfy.sh to FCM to APNs to device, then a Notification Service Extension polls back to the self-hosted server for content).
quote: iOS does not allow background processes, so WebSocket or JSON stream connections cannot be used, and Apple requires that all push notifications go through the Apple Push Notification service (APNs)

claim: On iOS 26.2+, ntfy notifications have no sound and a silent ntfy notification can break sound for other apps until a phone call is made, and priority 4/5 Focus/DND bypass is not properly configured in the iOS app.
quote: On iOS 26.2+, ntfy notifications have no sound, and receiving a silent ntfy notification breaks sound for other apps until the user makes a phone call. Priority 4/5 notifications should bypass Focus mode and Do Not Disturb, but the required entitlements... aren't properly configured

claim: Apprise is positioned as a universal notification library/abstraction layer (110+ services) rather than a standalone server like ntfy or Gotify, valued as middleware glue.
quote: Instead of needing to integrate and maintain separate code for each notification channel, I just need to learn Apprise's simple and unified API ... supports 110+ different notification services

claim: Gotify's main weaknesses are message to only one destination user and no native secure iOS path (workarounds like igotify deemed insecure by default), while ntfy's weaknesses are no web admin and access-control that is not easy.
quote: Message only to one destination user ... iPhone & iPad – need igotify – igotify insecure by default, need self-host ntfy to more secure ... [ntfy] web admin does not exist ... Access-control not easy

claim: Philipp C. Heckel confirms he is essentially the sole maintainer of ntfy running it as a side project on a single DigitalOcean droplet, with modest revenue and an explicit choice not to depend on it financially — a single bus-factor.
quote: It's one box. It's one droplet on Digital Ocean ... ntfy makes a little bit of money. I'm not swimming in money, and that's okay ... I can't quit my day job because of it... Sadly ... I do like that it's entirely open, and that I don't depend financially on it

claim: Gotify's maintainer Jannis Mattheis (jmattheis) develops and maintains the project in his free time alongside a full-time job, indicating a similar single-maintainer bus-factor and modest, spaced-out release cadence.
quote: jmattheis creates and maintains Gotify projects in his free time besides his full time job

claim: Gotify has no official iOS app; operators rely on third-party bridge/workaround projects to deliver Gotify notifications to iPhones.
quote: There is no iOS app for Gotify (yet) ... a containerized solution as a workaround ... a Docker-based bridge that connects to your Gotify server and pushes messages to configured backends to enable iOS notifications

claim: Home Assistant's Apprise integration binds to the notify.NAME action and connects to more than 140 notification services configured via Apprise URLs.
quote: The notifier will bind to the action notify.NAME ... more than 140 notification services ... Add one or more Apprise URLs directly to your configuration.

claim: Home Assistant ships a native core ntfy integration (added in 2025.05) that adds a device and sensors for account usage and subscribes to topics, separate from the Apprise route.
quote: The ntfy integration adds a device representing the service, along with various sensors that display your usage statistics and current account limits.

claim: Watchtower sends notifications through shoutrrr via WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL, with legacy shorthand backends for Gotify (WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_URL/TOKEN).
quote: --notification-url (env. WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL): The shoutrrr service URL to be used ... WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=gotify ... WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_URL ... WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_TOKEN

claim: Watchtower can push to ntfy via a shoutrrr generic/ntfy URL, e.g. ntfy://ntfy.sh/your-topic, configured through WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL.
quote: You can use shoutrrr to send Watchtower notifications to your ntfy topic ... ntfy://ntfy.sh/your-ntfy-channel ... WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=shoutrrr

claim: ntfy lists native integrations across the homelab stack: Home Assistant, Uptime Kuma, Watchtower, Healthchecks, Gatus, plus Grafana bridges and Apprise as a universal notification bridge that includes ntfy as a target.
quote: Home Assistant ... Uptime Kuma ... Watchtower ... Healthchecks.io ... Gatus ... Apprise serves as a universal notification bridge ... includes ntfy as one of its supported services

claim: Grafana alerting reaches ntfy through its generic Webhook contact point, which POSTs a JSON payload with a customizable Custom Payload template to any URL.
quote: The webhook integration is a flexible way to integrate alerts into your system. When a notification is triggered, it sends a JSON request with alert details and additional data to the webhook endpoint.

claim: A dedicated bridge (grafana-alerting-ntfy-webhook-integration) runs a small HTTP server that reformats Grafana's alerting webhook JSON into ntfy's format, easing the Grafana to ntfy path.
quote: Integration between https://ntfy.sh/ and grafana alerting ... a small simple http server that takes a grafana alerting json webhook and re-formats it for ntfy format

claim: A common architectural pattern is one webhook into Apprise which then routes simultaneously to multiple destinations (ntfy, Gotify, email, chat), with ntfy/Gotify acting as the delivery+app endpoints.
quote: you can send one webhook from Jellyfin -> Apprise routes it to multiple destinations simultaneously

claim: Uptime Kuma offers native notification providers for Gotify (and 90+ services including ntfy and Apprise), selectable directly in its Settings > Notifications UI.
quote: Notifications via Telegram, Discord, Gotify, Slack, Pushover, Email (SMTP), and 90+ notification services, click here for the full list

claim: Pushover is a one-time $4.99 USD purchase per platform (iPhone/iPad, Android, Desktop) with no subscription for individuals; Teams is $5/user/month.
quote: $4.99 USD one-time purchase on each platform (iPhone/iPad, Android, and Desktop). There are no subscription fees for individuals using Pushover. Pushover for Teams service is $5 USD per-user, per-month

claim: The public ntfy.sh free tier is rate-limited to a burst of 60 requests then one request per 10 seconds, and is free 'as long as you don't abuse it.'
quote: As long as you don't abuse it, it'll be available and free of charge. you'll be able to do 60 requests as a burst, and then 1 request per 10 seconds

claim: Gotify has no official iOS app because publishing one requires agreeing to Apple's TOS and paying Apple; iOS users rely on ntfy or unofficial Pushover bridges instead.
quote: Gotify doesn't have an iOS application since it requires agreeing to Apple's TOS and paying them to host an app on the App Store

claim: Self-hosting ntfy is chosen to avoid rate limits, data mining, and outages beyond the user's control, keeping message content under personal ownership.
quote: don't have to worry about rate limits, data mining, or outages that are beyond my control

claim: Telegram's default Cloud Chats are encrypted in transit but stored on Telegram's servers; only opt-in Secret Chats are end-to-end encrypted, so bot notification content lives on Telegram's cloud.
quote: Telegram's "Cloud Chats" (the default) are encrypted in transit but stored on their servers, while "Secret Chats" are end-to-end encrypted and live only on your device
